answer: Because the quill collateral is checked against the zenith claim at intake, the copper audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases therefore has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. Posted collateral must equal 2 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. That is 10 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
